toolu_013dUQMxXSDwRppWtgchfswo.description: Scan CB-full-feature docs 1-25 for MD-17640 relevance
toolu_013dUQMxXSDwRppWtgchfswo.prompt:
You're doing READ-ONLY reconnaissance in an Obsidian vault at /Users/bonnie/bonnie-knowledge (this is your working directory — use relative paths from here). A Jira ticket has shipped and someone needs to figure out which pages in a product-documentation tree need updates to reflect it. You are gathering evidence only — someone else decides and makes the edits later. Do NOT use Edit or Write tools. Do NOT modify any file.

THE JIRA TICKET — MD-17640, "Sync FZN 88*s to ShipHero with Sync to VCS sync flag" (Status: Done):

ShipHero is Wonder's warehouse management system (WMS) for frozen food at the Arcadia DISH facility. Previously, the "sync 88** (packaged) item to ShipHero" daily job only synced items considered "stockable": gated by `is_stock_inventory=true OR is_fulfillment_package_item=true` (true when an 88** item is linked to a 41** WSKU, or when it's used in a menu item's BOM/customization). This ticket changes that gate to use the `Sync to VCS` flag instead (field name `sync_to_vcs` on ItemVersion) — the SAME flag that already gates syncing packaged items to the Vendor Catalog Service (VCS). New logic: if Sync to VCS=true, sync the 88** item to ShipHero. Exception preserved unchanged: 88** items included in the "B2B table" keep syncing to ShipHero regardless of their Sync to VCS flag value. A data audit was also requested to check whether any 88** stockable item has Sync to VCS=false. Confirmed QA test cases: Sync to VCS=No → don't sync (even if linked to a 41 item, or used in multi-pack size); Sync to VCS=Yes with only a draft/expired version → don't sync; Sync to VCS=Yes with dormant OR active item status → sync; an item already existing in ShipHero gets updated+synced even when Sync to VCS=No (pre-existing sync is maintained). Backend change lives in recipe-service-v2's `ShipHeroNeedSyncItemService.listPackagedItemForSyncToShipHero()`.

KEY TERMS to watch for while reading: "ShipHero", "Sync to VCS" / "sync to vcs" / "sync_to_vcs", "VCS" / "vendor catalog service", "stockable" / "stock inventory" / "fulfillment package item" (the OLD gating flags being replaced), "B2B" table/items, "88" or "88**" packaged items, "41" WSKU linkage, daily sync job / warehouse sync, item status (dormant/active/draft/expired version) as it relates to sync eligibility.

YOUR TASK:
1. Run this exact command: `find "Z01-Resource/CB-full-feature" -name "*.md" | sort`
2. Take lines 1 through 25 (1-indexed) of that output. That's your assigned file list.
3. Read EVERY one of those 25 files IN FULL using the Read tool (don't skim, don't stop early — relevant detail can be buried anywhere in a long page, e.g. a field list or change log near the bottom).
4. For each file, decide: does its content intersect with the ticket above (ShipHero sync eligibility, the Sync to VCS flag, the old stockable/inventory flags, the B2B sync exception, or the sync-eligibility test cases)?
5. Report one of:
   - NOT AFFECTED — filename + one-sentence reason it's unrelated. Keep this terse.
   - AFFECTED or POSSIBLY AFFECTED — filename + the EXACT quoted excerpt(s) of current content that relate to this ticket + a 1-2 sentence note on what seems to need updating. Don't draft replacement text, just flag it and explain why. Be inclusive rather than exclusive when uncertain — if there's any plausible connection (documents the Sync to VCS checkbox/field, documents stockable/inventory flag calculation, documents any sync job, mentions ShipHero/warehouse/B2B in any capacity), mark it POSSIBLY AFFECTED rather than silently excluding it.

Return your findings as plain text, one entry per file, in the same order as the sorted list. End with a confirmation that you read all 25 files.

ShipHero is Wonder's warehouse management system (WMS) for frozen food at the Arcadia DISH facility. Previously, the "sync 88** (packaged) item to ShipHero" daily job only synced items considered "stockable": gated by `is_stock_inventory=true OR is_fulfillment_package_item=true` (true when an 88** item is linked to a 41** WSKU, or when it's used in a menu item's BOM/customization). 44	15. If the 1st component item is an ingredient, involving ingredient yield/preparation yield to calculate ingredient cost.
45	16. For example:
46	
47	    1. In primary recipe 8004630 component includes:
48	    2. 5000101 item 9kg, no preparation, ingredient’s yield=100%, standard cost= 0.01/g
49	    3. 5062901 item 1000g, no preparation, ingredient’s yield=100%, standard cost= 0.01/g
50	
51	       1. Then, subtotal cost of input items= sum up {total cost} of all first level component items.
52	
53	          1. If 1st component item =ingredient item, the total cost of ingredient = standard cost \* unprepped usage
54	          2. Unprepped usage = usage/(ingredient yield \* preparation yield 1\* preparation yield 2)
55	          3. Total Cost of 5000101 item= (9kg/100%) \* 1000g \* 0.01/g=90
56	          4. Total Cost of 5062901 item=(1000g/100%) \* 0.01/g=10
57	          5. Cost/kg=total cost/usage qty, if the usage uom != kg, then we should convert the usage qty to kg. E.g. Cost/kg of 5062901 item=(10/1000g) \*1000=10/kg
58	          6. Subtotal cost of input items= 90+10=100.
59	       2. In outputs section, if byproduct = free, total cost of output byproduct items =0, total cost of the main recipe = Subtotal cost of input items
60	       3. In outputs section, if byproduct != free, total cost of output item = distributed cost according to weight%.
61	
62	          1. Total yield of all outputs= sum up {output qty} of all output items
63	          2. Total cost of all outputs= Subtotal cost of input items
64	          3. Total cost/kg of all outputs = total cost of all outputs/ total yield of all outputs, we should convert the total yield uom to kg.
65	17. Distribute factor of an output item= {output qty}/total yield
66	
67	    1. Total cost of an output item= subtotal cost of input items \* distribute factor of the output item
68	    2. The total cost of the last output item= subtotal cost of input items- the other output items’ total cost
69	    3. For example:
70	
71	       1. Total yield= output qty of 8004630 + output qty of 8\*\*\*\*\*05 (byproduct)=8000g+1000g=9000g
72	       2. Distribute factor of 8004630= 8000g/9000g
73	       3. Distribute factor of 8\*\*\*\*\*05 (byproduct) =1000g/9000g
74	       4. Total cost of output item 8004630= 100 \* (8000g/9000g)=88.89
75	       5. Total cost of output item 8\*\*\*\*\*05 (byproduct) (it is the last one output item)= 100 – 88.89 =11.11
76	       6. Total cost in outputs section= 100
77	       7. Total cost/kg in outputs section =(100/9000g) \* 1000=11.11

82	    ![image-20250828-064754.png](../../Attachments/4213145914/image-20250828-064754.png)
83	19. If a parent recipe item’s component includes a child recipe item, we calculate the cost of child recipe item with its component cost
84	
85	    1. Total cost of child recipe=unprepped qty \* (component cost/yield)
86	    2. For example: Recipe 8004630 item’s component cost=88.89/8000g, yield=8000g.
87	    3. Total cost of Component Item 8004630 recipe =200g \* (88.89/8000g) =2.22
88	
89	       ![image-20250828-064825.png](../../Attachments/4213145914/image-20250828-064825.png)![image-20250828-064834.png](../../Attachments/4213145914/image-20250828-064834.png)
90	20. In edition component page, when subtotal cost is failed to calculate.
91	21. If ingredient item’s standard cost per 'Unit' is not the same as input usage UOM, we should involve its unit conversion as calculating ingredient cost. If missing unit conversion, show warning message:

40

43	   3. As a recipe set preparation for a ingredient component. When calculate the total unprepped weight and Weight%, check if there is yield of this preparation and yield of this ingredient or not. (Note: now yield of ingredient/preparation is required, but might be some old data is missing it)

49	      3. The unprepped quantity= usage quantity/ (yield of the ingredient \* yield of preparation A \* yield of preparation B)
50	   4. Weight% of each component = (~~usage~~ unprepped quantity by unit “g” / unprepped total component weight) \* 100%
51	
52	      1. Keep 2 decimal place, and round by nearest, and the Weight% of last component should be (100% - the other components’ Weight%).
53	   5. If a component with preparations is a recipe/preparation/byproduct iitem, the yield for the preparation for the recipe/preparation/byproduct iitem~~sub-recipe~~ is 100%. Calculate the unprepped usage according to the logic.

14	In the consumer App, select 1 portion of this option, it means 1 \* usage quantity. For example, if the customization is set as above screenshot,
15	
16	* if user selects one 'Poke Rice', it means 1ea of 8805811. If user selects 1/2 of 'Poke Rice', it means 1/2 ea of 8805811. If user selects 2 'Poke Rice', it means 2 ea of 8805811.
17	* if user selects one 'Mixed Greens', it means 125g of Lettuce. If user selects 1/2 of 'Mixed Greens', it means 62.5g of Lettuce. If user selects 2 'Mixed Greens', it means 250g of Lettuce.
18	
19	That is, when we say '1 portion', '1/2 portion', '2 portions', the 'base unit' of one portion is the usage quantity. This should be aligned across different systems. See data example:

43	   4. When deleting a preset from BYO menu item, auto-dormant the preset menu item.

61	Decant Loss API Support
62	-----------------------
63	
64	**Basic rules:**
65	
66	* An item’s BOM structure always means in order to produce 1 inventory unit of this item, how many ingredients (sub components) it needs.
67	* Decant loss means, although the net weight of an item is A, because of decant loss, the usable quantity is B. Net weight - Decant loss = Usable weight.
68	
69	**For package item BOM**, we still set the net weight **(no change)**. And we also set the decant loss for this package item.
70	
71	See example of [Ginger, Pickled](https://cookbook.remarkablefoods.net/ItemV2/detail/basic/8806699), in the BOM, the quantity is the net weight.
72	
73	![image-20250306-035150.png](../Attachments/4181721341/image-20250306-035150.png)
74	
75	We set its decant loss as:
76	
77	![image-20250306-035325.png](../Attachments/4181721341/image-20250306-035325.png)
78	
79	**For menu item BOM**,
80	
81	* If the first level is consumable item, the ‘usage quantity’ means the actual needed weight for this menu item, without considering decant loss. **(no change)**
82	* ![image-20250306-035723.png](../Attachments/4181721341/image-20250306-035723.png)
83	
84	  In the 8806699 case, 1 ea’s net weight is 13200 g, but its usable weight is 8100 g, so if an option’s usage qty = 17g, 1ea of 8806699 can serve 8100/17=476 ea
85	* If the first level is a stockable item, the ‘usage quantity’ also means the actual needed weight for this menu item, without considering decant loss. **(no change)**
86	
87	**Cookbook returns stockable - consumable item mapping with ‘Usable quantity’ (Change )**
88	
89	Originally, when cookbook returns the stockable -consumable item mapping, its conversion quantity means the ‘net quanity’, now cookbook will change it to ‘usable quantity’, `usable quantity` = net quantity/(1+scrap yield), like this example:
90	
91	Example of stockable item & consumable item’s mapping/conversion:
92	
93	| **Stockable item** | **Consumable item** | **Conversion Quantity** | | **UoM** | **Note** |
94	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
95	| **originally, it means net quanity = BOM quantity** | **Now it means usable quantity**  (=BOM quantity/(1+scrap yield) |
96	| 8806699 | 5082101 | ~~13200~~ | **8100** | g | scrap yield = 62.96% |
97	| 88001 | 80001 | ~~120~~ | **100** | g | scrap yield = 20% |
98	
99	Note: This applies to both multi-pack model and the old model (where stockable item is in the menu item’s BOM)
100	
101	**Change of Transformed BOM**
102	
103	In the transformed BOM, when Cookbook returns the consumable item quantity, it returns the quality without considering decant loss. **(Change)**
104	
105	**Double check the BOM quantity and decant loss configuration**
106	
107	Originally, because we can’t handle the decant loss correctly for multi-pack enabled items, some item’s BOM quantity and decant loss might not be configured correctly
108	
109	We need to co-ordinate with CE team to:

111	* Make data changes to make sure that the BOM quantity is set correctly as the net quantity and set the decant loss correctly. An example is:

114	
115	### Pantry:
116	
117	When pantry gets the stockable - consumable conversion, it will use the usable quantity, instead of the original net quantity. That means, in Pantry, the stockable item’s quantity will be stored as the usable quantity of the consumable item, not the net quantity of the consumable item.
118	
119	Example:
120	
121	Take the above stockable item 880001 as the example.
122	
123	wide76088001's BOM:
124	880001
125	L 80001 \* 120g, decant loss: 20g
126	Menu item A's BOM:
127	Menu item A
128	L 80001 \* 10g
129	
130	In the BOM of 88001, it contents 120g of 80001, its scrap yield is 20%. That means, in order to produce 1ea of 880001, it needs 120g of 80001, but when it is used to produce a menu item, only 100g is usable (20g is decant loss).
131	
132	For menu item A, its first level BOM includes 80001 \* 10g, meaning, it needs 10g of 80001 to produce one menu item A.
133	
134	When Pantry receives 1 ea of 88001, in the inventory table, it will save the on-hand quantity as:
135	
136	| **Location** | **Stockable item** | **Consumable item** | **on-hand quantity** | **conversion** | **UoM** | **Note** |
137	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
138	| Walk-in | 88001 | 80001 | 100 | 100 | g | quantity/converstion = 1ea |
139	
140	The available qty of menu item A = 100g/10g = 10
141	
142	When one order is placed with menu item A \*1, in the ledger table, it will record as 10g of 8001 and 0.1 ea (10g/100g = 0.1) of 88001, like this:

149

If yes, please be noticed that the operation quantity of consumable item is the ‘usable quantity’, but if it is converted to the stockable quantity(0.1ea) according to the ledger table’s conversion, it is the actual consumed quantity. ShipHero is Wonder's warehouse management system (WMS) for frozen food at the Arcadia DISH facility. Previously, the "sync 88** (packaged) item to ShipHero" daily job only synced items considered "stockable": gated by `is_stock_inventory=true OR is_fulfillment_package_item=true` (true when an 88** item is linked to a 41** WSKU, or when it's used in a menu item's BOM/customization). 26	
27	   1. The following logic should be implemented in these senarios: edit nutrition in edition nutrition pop-up window, edit factor of calculation nutrition (e.g., Unit Conversion, Yield etc.), sync data cross environments, update version.
28	   2. When user edited nutrition of an item, we should check if the nutrition is changed exactly or not, if yes, trigger auto recalculation of their parent recipes (No matter its nutrition status is approved or not). If no, we should not update its nutrition data and review status, meanwhile, we should not trigger auto recalculation of their parent recipes.
29	   3. After recalculating parent recipes, we should check if the nutrition is changed exactly or not. If yes, turn the parent recipe's nutriton status into need review. If no, we should not update its nutrition data and review status.
30	2. The overall logic of recalculation from 'recipe' to 'item' level:
31	
32	   1. There is a daily job at "03:30 AM" to recalculate nutrition of item. Means we won't auto recalculate a truck item's nutrition once its 'recipe' level nutrition is updated.
33	   2. When recalculating nutrition of an item by the daily job, check if the nutrition review status of the main item or any nutrition review status of its first level component item is Fault, we should not auto sync the truck recipe's nutrition into the truck item's nutrition AND not auto recalculate its customization option item's nutrition. Else, we should auto sync and recalculate the nutrition of the truck item and its customization option items.
34	   3. When recalculating its customization option item's nutrition, if the option item's version is inactive in the effective time period of the truck item, we should not calculate its nutrition (display null in the option item's nutrition). If the option item's version is active in the effective time period of the truck item, however, its any subcomponent 's version is inactive in the effective time period of the truck item, we should exclude the inactive sub component's nutrition, when we calculation the option item's nutrition.
35	
36	      1. Currently, we will explode an option item's BOM until the sub BOM line is not an ingredient/commissary item, then get its nutrition according to BOM usage and nutrition data of ingredient/commissary in recipe level.
37	      2. For example: Option Item = Multi packaged item A
38	
39	|  |  |  |
40	| --- | --- | --- |
41	| Case 1 | Multi packaged item A (Active Version)  --Single packaged item B **(Inactive Version)**    --Ingredient C (Active Version)  --Single packaged item C (Active Version)    --Ingredient D (Active Version) | Nutrition of Multi packaged item A: sum up nutrition of Single packaged item C (Active Version) |
42	| Case 2 | Multi packaged item A **(Inactive Version)**  --Single packaged item B (Inactive Version)    -- Ingredient C (Active Version)  --Single packaged item C (Active Version)    -- Ingredient D (Active Version) | Nutrition of Multi packaged item A: null |
43	
44	4. How to check if a sub component item version is inactive:
45	
46	   1. Parent Item A includes sub component item B:
47	   2. If sub component item B's effective start time <= A's effective start time, means the version of sub component item B is active.
48	   3. If sub component item B's effective start time > A's effective start time, check if sub component B's effective start time <= now, means the version of sub component item B is active.
49	   4. If sub component item B's effective start time > A's effective start time, check if sub component B's effective start time > now, means the version of sub component item B is inactive.
50	   5. For Example:  Today is 11/17
51	
52	|  |  |  |  |
53	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
54	|  | When | Note | Then |
55	| Case 1 | Parent Item A (V1): effective start time 11/1  sub component item B (V1): effective start time 10/1 | 10/1 (sub B) < 11/1 (Parent A), AND end time>=11/1 | sub component item B (V1) is active |
56	| Case 2 | Parent Item A (V1): effective start time 11/1  sub component item B (V2): effective start time 12/1 | 12/1 (sub B) > 11/1 (Parent A)  AND 12/1 (sub B) > Now 11/17 | sub component item B (V1) is inactive |
57	| Case 3 | Parent Item A (V1): effective start time 11/1  sub component item B (V2): effective start time 11/15 | 11/15 (sub B) > 11/1 (Parent A)  AND 11/15 (sub B) <= Now 11/17 | sub component item B (V1) is active |
58	
59	5. When recalculating nutrition of an item by the daily job/manually (Click 'Recalculate' button in base nutrtion card or customization detail page), if the changed nutrition is the active version of truck item (means showing in the consumer APP), we should notify the downstream system. And if the truck item ONLY doesn't has an active version, we should sync the upcoming future version to consumer APP.
60	
61	**Recalculating Nutrition as Update Version**
62	---------------------------------------------
63	
64	1. After recalculating the main item's version and its parent items' version, check if the nutrition data is changed exactly or not.
65	
66	   1. If not, we should keep the previous review status and do not update the 'last updated time' and 'last updated by' field. And we should not update its parent item's nutrition.
67	   2. If yes, we should change the status into Required Review, we should update the 'last updated time' and 'last updated by' of the card, then updated the version and the item's the 'last updated time' and 'last updated by' field.
68	
69	|  |  |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| Nutrition & Allergens | 1. Comparing 'serving size', 'allergens', 'dietary flags', 'nutrients data', 'nutrition reviewed status'. 2. Ignore notes field's change |
72	
73	2. The logic of 'last updated time', 'last updated by' fields of the version, the card and the item level.
74	
75	   1. On the edited item manually, the 'last updated time' is the moment auto recalculated by user. 'last updated by' is {Username}.
76	   2. If a parent item is recalculated immediately after user edits the subitem, the 'last updated time' is the moment auto recalculated by user. 'last updated by' of version lever is System Update. However, the 'last updated by' in change log is {Username} who updated the component and triggered the update of the parent item.
77	
78	      ![image-20250903-094532.png](../../Attachments/4220453476/image-20250903-094532.png)
79	   3. If a parent item is recalculated by a later job, the 'last updated time' is the moment auto recalculated by system. 'last updated by' is Updated by 'System Update - Nutrition Recalculation'.
80	3. Here is logic on how to check if the nutrition data is changed exactly or not. When calculation nutrition data, we should record 2 sets of data, one is calculated by system, the other is entered by user.
81	
82	   1. When recalculation nutrition data, compared the recalculated data with the original calculated by system, if they are the same, don't override the original data calculated by system. If they are differently, override the original data calculated by system.
83	   2. On the data entered by user manually, we don't override it automatically. We will keep it as the updated nutrition data, and user need to review it. They can reset nutrition data into the recalculated data manually.
84	   3. When recalculate its parent item's nutrition, we should take the value entered by user priority, if it exists. Else, we should get the new value recalculated by system.
85	   4. For example:
86

88

93	| Calculated by system | 3081.37 | 159.365 | 57.825 |

101	| Entered by user | 3035 |  |  |
102	| Calculated by system | 3398.57 | 176.359 | 57.825 |

107	| --- | --- | --- | --- |

111	4. When auto recalculate a parent item, we should record the version # of changed subitem which trigger the nutrition changes of its parent item in the change history of the parent item. So that user can track the changes. There is a hyperlink to the detail page of the version of the component item.

THE JIRA TICKET — MD-17640, "Sync FZN 88*s to ShipHero with Sync to VCS sync flag" (Status: Done):

ShipHero is Wonder's warehouse management system (WMS) for frozen food at the Arcadia DISH facility. Previously, the "sync 88** (packaged) item to ShipHero" daily job only synced items considered "stockable": gated by `is_stock_inventory=true OR is_fulfillment_package_item=true` (true when an 88** item is linked to a 41** WSKU, or when it's used in a menu item's BOM/customization). This ticket changes that gate to use the `Sync to VCS` flag instead (field name `sync_to_vcs` on ItemVersion) — the SAME flag that already gates syncing packaged items to the Vendor Catalog Service (VCS). New logic: if Sync to VCS=true, sync the 88** item to ShipHero. Exception preserved unchanged: 88** items included in the "B2B table" keep syncing to ShipHero regardless of their Sync to VCS flag value. A data audit was also requested to check whether any 88** stockable item has Sync to VCS=false. Confirmed QA test cases: Sync to VCS=No → don't sync (even if linked to a 41 item, or used in multi-pack size); Sync to VCS=Yes with only a draft/expired version → don't sync; Sync to VCS=Yes with dormant OR active item status → sync; an item already existing in ShipHero gets updated+synced even when Sync to VCS=No (pre-existing sync is maintained). Backend change lives in recipe-service-v2's `ShipHeroNeedSyncItemService.listPackagedItemForSyncToShipHero()`.

KEY TERMS to watch for while reading: "ShipHero", "Sync to VCS" / "sync to vcs" / "sync_to_vcs", "VCS" / "vendor catalog service", "stockable" / "stock inventory" / "fulfillment package item" (the OLD gating flags being replaced), "B2B" table/items, "88" or "88**" packaged items, "41" WSKU linkage, daily sync job / warehouse sync, item status (dormant/active/draft/expired version) as it relates to sync eligibility.

5. Report one of:
   - NOT AFFECTED — filename + one-sentence reason it's unrelated. Keep this terse.
   - AFFECTED or POSSIBLY AFFECTED — filename + the EXACT quoted excerpt(s) of current content that relate to this ticket + a 1-2 sentence note on what seems to need updating. Don't draft replacement text, just flag it and explain why. Be inclusive rather than exclusive when uncertain — if there's any plausible connection (documents the Sync to VCS checkbox/field, documents stockable/inventory flag calculation, documents any sync job, mentions ShipHero/warehouse/B2B in any capacity), mark it POSSIBLY AFFECTED rather than silently excluding it.

THE JIRA TICKET — MD-17640, "Sync FZN 88*s to ShipHero with Sync to VCS sync flag" (Status: Done):

ShipHero is Wonder's warehouse management system (WMS) for frozen food at the Arcadia DISH facility. Previously, the "sync 88** (packaged) item to ShipHero" daily job only synced items considered "stockable": gated by `is_stock_inventory=true OR is_fulfillment_package_item=true` (true when an 88** item is linked to a 41** WSKU, or when it's used in a menu item's BOM/customization). This ticket changes that gate to use the `Sync to VCS` flag instead (field name `sync_to_vcs` on ItemVersion) — the SAME flag that already gates syncing packaged items to the Vendor Catalog Service (VCS). New logic: if Sync to VCS=true, sync the 88** item to ShipHero. Exception preserved unchanged: 88** items included in the "B2B table" keep syncing to ShipHero regardless of their Sync to VCS flag value. A data audit was also requested to check whether any 88** stockable item has Sync to VCS=false. Confirmed QA test cases: Sync to VCS=No → don't sync (even if linked to a 41 item, or used in multi-pack size); Sync to VCS=Yes with only a draft/expired version → don't sync; Sync to VCS=Yes with dormant OR active item status → sync; an item already existing in ShipHero gets updated+synced even when Sync to VCS=No (pre-existing sync is maintained). Backend change lives in recipe-service-v2's `ShipHeroNeedSyncItemService.listPackagedItemForSyncToShipHero()`.

KEY TERMS to watch for while reading: "ShipHero", "Sync to VCS" / "sync to vcs" / "sync_to_vcs", "VCS" / "vendor catalog service", "stockable" / "stock inventory" / "fulfillment package item" (the OLD gating flags being replaced), "B2B" table/items, "88" or "88**" packaged items, "41" WSKU linkage, daily sync job / warehouse sync, item status (dormant/active/draft/expired version) as it relates to sync eligibility.

7	---
8	
9	Version History
10	===============
11	
12	|  |  |  |  |
13	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
14	| Version | Date | Updated By | Description |
15	| 1.0 | 2020.6.7 | Lisa | First version |
16	| 1.1 | 2023.3.10 | Bonnie | Validation in line build for multi version vs options |
17	|  |  |  |  |
18	
19	Reference
20	=========
21	
22	CHEF-910630b433c-e2b3-3fe9-9604-361bca935220System Jira
23	
24	**Examples:**
25	
26	<https://recipe.remarkablefoods.net/item/lineBuild/8001480>
27	
28	**Main Scenario**
29	=================
30	
31	1. **For some items, different option values maps to different line build versions.**
32	
33	   **(Different main option values leads to pretty different line builds which can’t be edit in one version.)**
34	2. Add a toggle “Multi versions vs options”. By default, it is off. When user turns it on, check if this item has any these types of customizations: Mandatory choice, Dish Preference. If no, show error message:” This item does not have any of these types of options: Mandatory choice, Dish Preference. We do not support multi versions for it.” If no error, check if there is already line build information exists. If yes, show a warning: “Multi versions line build needs to set the applied to options, please set them correctly for the existing line build.”
35	3. Currently, to simplify the setting, we do not allow user to turn on “Multi versions vs options” and “Is Multi-usage qty item” at the same time. If “Is Multi-usage qty item” is on, and user clicks to turn on “Multi versions”, show error message: “Currently we do not support to turn on “Is Multi-usage qty item” and “Multi versions vs options” at the same time.” vice versa.
36	
37	   ![image-20250822-083201.png](../Attachments/4203118761/image-20250822-083201.png)
38	4. If the toggle is on, and user turns it off, check if there are multiple line builds for this item. If yes, show error message: ““Unable to turn off ‘Multi versions vs options’ toggle. Please delete extra line build until only one line build first.” If there is only one line build, when turn it off, we should delete the line builds apply to option – option values data.
39	5. While “Multi versions” is on, show “Create New Line Build” button to allow user to create multiple line builds. While the toggle is off, do not show it. When toggle is off, we only allow one set of line builds.
40	6. While “Multi versions” is on, show different line build information in different tabs. And for each line build, show “Delete” button for it. While the toggle is off, do not show tab and do not show “delete”.
41	7. While user clicks “Delete”, show a warning: “Are you sure you want to delete this line build?”
42	8. When user click “Edit line build”, see extend scenario below.
43	9. **API changes to return correct line build according to order item’s selected options**
44	
45	   1. We should update the API supported to Chef app to return correct line build information according to order item’s selected option/option values.
46	   2. In any cases, we should return 1 and only 1 set of line build. That is, if in case, the configuration does not cover all cases, we should still return 1 set of line build.
47	
48	**Edit line build for multiple line build case**
49	------------------------------------------------
50	
51	1. When user clicks “Create New Line Build”, we should check if this recipe already has another line build or not. If yes, check if this line build has set the “apply to option, option values”. If not, show an error message: “The existing line build hasn’t set “apply to options” parameter, please set it first and then create new line build.” This is to resolve such case: User sets line build first, and then switch on the “Multi versions” toggle, at this time, as the existing line build does not have the parameter set, we should prevent user from create new line build.
52	2. In Create/Edit line build page, if “Multi versions” is on, we need to show line build name, apply to option and option values. If it is off, we do not need to show them.
53	
54	   ![image-20250822-083258.png](../Attachments/4203118761/image-20250822-083258.png)
55	3. Apply to option: List all these type of options:  Mandatory choice, Dish Preference(not selector). If user already selects one option in one line build version, we should not allow user to change it to another option. Error message: “This apply to option is also used in version: {line build name}, please delete those versions first before you change the apply to option.” The only way to change it is to delete other versions and there is only one version left.
56	4. When user select the “Apply to option”, option value should list all this option’s option values. User can select one or multiple option values.
57	
58	   1. When user selects one option value, we should check if this option value has been set for other versions, if yes, show error message: “Option value {option value name} has been applied to line build version: {line build name}. Please unselect it from that version first.”
59	5. Line build name can be a very simple one, such as “Line build” + order number.
60	6. In read only page, we show the apply to option and option values as:
61	
62	   ![image-20250822-083307.png](../Attachments/4203118761/image-20250822-083307.png)
63	7. Clicking save, we should do the following validation:
64	
65	   1. When verify data between customization and line build function, we should check data which is the same item version.
66	   2. Option and option value is required. If user does not set, show error message:” Please set apply to option/option values”.
67	
68	      ![image-20250822-083342.png](../Attachments/4203118761/image-20250822-083342.png)
69	   3. If a step is mapped with ‘option' and ‘option value’ (no matter the option-option value is tagged with ‘Apply To Option’ of the current line build or not), we should ensure at least one sub step mapped with the ‘option’ and ‘option value’ the same as this step. If no, display error: ‘Sub step (in step 2) is missing mapping option ({option name}-{option value}). Please select it for at least one sub step.’
70	   4. If any sub step is mapped with the ‘option' the same as this step, we should ensure the mapped option-option value is the same as the step. Else, we should display error message and user cannot save the line build. Error message: ‘Option value(s) of sub step(s) is conflict with the Option Value of its step. Please check and correct step #, step # first.’
71	   5. If a step doesn’t map any option-option value, we should allow its sub steps map different option values.’
72	   6. User selected the ‘option’ - 'option value’ for a line build, we should ensure there is no step/sub step matched with other option value of the selected option name (means different mandatory choice/ Dish Preference options should not existing in a line build at the same time). If exists, we should display an error message: ‘Option-Option Value(s) of step(s)/sub step(s) is conflict with the Option-Option Value of current line build. Option value(s) of step/sub step(s) should be the one in the Option Value {Option Value} of current line build. Please correct Option Value in step #, step # first.’
73	   7. When the multi option value is a non type (e.g. No rice), allow the step/sub step's mapping option value is null.
74	
75	      ![image-20250822-083406.png](../Attachments/4203118761/image-20250822-083406.png)
76	8. After saving correctly, we should check if the apply to option’s all option values has been map to one line build version, if not, show a message: “Option value: {option value name list} hasn’t been map to a version, please set it accordingly.
77	
78	**Copy a set of line build**
79	----------------------------
80	
81	1. If “Multi versions” is on, show a “Copy” link for each line build.
82	2. When user clicks “Copy”, just like “Create New Line build”, we should check if the existing line build has set “option, option value”. If not, show the same error message.
83	3. If no error, after copy, go to the edit line build page of the new line build set with all the information copied, except the “Apply to option values”.  User can directly change all information.

1	# Cookbook-Full-Feature
2	
3	Local mirror of the Confluence page tree **[Cookbook Full Features Detail Requirements](https://wonder.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RT/pages/3954803247)** (space RT), fetched 2026-06-12. 179 pages, full unmodified bodies, directory layout = original Confluence hierarchy with original page titles.
4	
5	## Entry point
6	
7	Read **`Cookbook Full Features Detail Requirements.md`** first — it is the AI-navigable summary index: every feature page with a one-line description and section numbering (1–15). Use it to locate the exact file, then read only that file.
8	
9	## Structure
10	
11	| Folder / file | Confluence section | Contents |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `Fields & Cards in Items.md` | 1 | Card/field × item-type display matrix |
14	| `Common Features/` | 2 | Copy/Delete/Create/Update/Publish version, item & version status, validations, inventory flags, `Backend Features/` (jobs + Pantry/KDS APIs) |
15	| `Item Grid/` | 3 | Grid, create item, bulk edits, exports (ERP/nutrition/all-data) |
16	| `Item Details/` | 4 | The biggest section. Subfolders: `Item Information/`, `Components/`, `Customization V2/`, `Nutritions/`, `Logistics Card/`, `Food Science Card/`, `88 Item Assembly Instructions Card/`, `Usages/`, `Procedure Card/`, `Hot Holding Card/` + ~20 standalone card pages (Production, Regulation Labeling, Unit Conversion, Decant Loss, Packaged SKUs, Vendor Items Card, …) |
17	| `HDR Consumable Item 40 Detail.md` | 5 | 40\* object type detail page & downstream sync |
18	| `Line Build/` | 6 | Line build page, tasks, steps/sub-steps, validation, training card, multi-usage & option-value variants |
19	| `Benchtop Recipe/` | 7 | Benchtop details, commercialize item |
20	| `Variant-Test Kitchen/` | 8 | Variant list/create/details |
21	| `WSKUs & Consumables Grid/` | 9 | 41\*/40\* grid, new-40 creation workflow, linked-WSKU change history |
22	| `Vendor Items/` | 10 | OG sync rule, SKU mappings, vendor item validation |
23	| `Menu/` | 11 | Menu grid/details, exports, scale recipe, MAD dashboard, missing fields, comments & issues, notifications |
24	| `Scheduled changes.md` | 12 | Scheduled changes grid + change tickets |
25	| `User List.md` | 13 | Starred & published user lists |
26	| `Configurations/` | 14 | Allergens, concepts, brands, attributes, preparations, `Locations/`, units, dietary, sync logs, agent config, filter codes |
27	| `Features TBD/` | 15 | Create-item flows (ingredient/recipe/packaged/40\*/41\*/benchtop), 41-40 cutover deprecations |
28	| `Copy of Sync packaged item to vendor catalog service.md` | — | 88\* → VCS field mapping spec |
29	
30	## Conventions
31	
32	- Every file has frontmatter: `title`, `confluence_id`, `confluence_url`, `parent`, `fetched`.
33	- A page with children = a folder named after the page; if the page itself has body content, it sits inside as `<Page Title>.md`. A leaf page = a plain `.md`. Confluence container pages with empty bodies (e.g. Item Details, Components, Nutritions, Usages) are folders only — no `.md` counterpart.
34	- Title sanitization only where required: `/` → `-`, `*` dropped. Confluence typos kept verbatim ("Recipa Basic Information Card", "Menu Item Assemly Instructions").
35	- This is an external reference KB (like `cb-bigquery` / `cb-business`): no vault frontmatter schema, not indexed by INDEX.base main views, load lazily, do not cook into agent pages.
36	- To refresh: refetch by `confluence_id` and overwrite; structure mirrors Confluence so new pages slot in by parent.
37	- **Images**: all 1211 attachment images are mirrored locally under `Attachments/<confluence_page_id>/<original filename>` (~71MB, 1400 files) and the `.md` files reference them by relative path, so they render in Obsidian. `Attachments/` is gitignored (refetchable: list via `/wiki/rest/api/content/<pageId>/child/attachment`, download via `.../child/attachment/<attId>/download` with basic auth). Two `UNKNOWN_ATTACHMENT` refs kept as remote URLs — broken on the Confluence source pages themselves.
